review_notes: I read the whole file and searched the SLELocalization directory for simp attributes and for uses of the initial-value lemmas. The directory has only a few @[simp] lemmas (SlitMaps, DyadicKernels, ConformalKernels). None are in this file, and none cover the BoundaryFunctional evaluation lemmas. Almost all of GreenTilts is long proof-chains with explicit rewrites, so I found no competing rules or loops in it. The two findings are the evaluation-at-zero lemmas, which are repeatedly listed by hand in `simp only` calls. I did not run Lean. Whether `@[simp]` would fire on every call site is untested; in particular, call sites where position/logDerivative appear after unfolding a definition may still need the explicit list.

findings.excerpt:
lemma position_initial {ε T : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) (hT : 0 ≤ T)
    (U : C(I, ℝ)) (z : ℂ) : position hε hT U z 0 = z := by
findings.problem: This unconditional, terminating, shrinking evaluation lemma (`position … 0 = z`) is not tagged `@[simp]`. Every client has to name it by hand inside `simp only [...]`. It appears in the same 'initial' bundle with `logDerivative_initial` in LoewnerFlow, AngularClock, SwallowingLaws, ConditionalTilts and BoundaryDiffusion. It is also used in this file at lines 49, 353-355, and elsewhere. The only canonical simp normal form for `position … 0` is therefore reached by an ad-hoc lemma list.
findings.proposed_change: Add `@[simp]` to `position_initial`. The LHS has the form `position hε hT U z 0`, with the proof arguments `hε` and `hT` as implicit-by-unification arguments. The RHS `z` is a strict simplification, so no cycle is possible. Call sites like `simpa only [position_initial] using hh` can then shorten to `simpa using hh`, and `simp only [field, height, position_initial, logDerivative_initial, …]` can drop the two initial-value lemmas.
findings.benefit: The initial-value normal form comes automatically from `simp`. Downstream `simp only` lists get shorter. New proofs about the Loewner cutoff flow at time 0 do not need to remember to add the lemma.

findings.excerpt:
lemma logDerivative_initial {ε T : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) (hT : 0 ≤ T)
    (U : C(I, ℝ)) (z : ℂ) : logDerivative hε hT U z 0 = 0 := by
findings.problem: `logDerivative … 0 = 0` is an unconditional evaluation lemma that rewrites to a literal. It is not marked `@[simp]`. It is always used together with `position_initial`, `mul_zero`, `Real.exp_zero`, etc., in explicit `simp only` lists. For example, `radius … 0` needs `logDerivative_initial` followed by `Real.exp_zero` and `div_one`. Because `logDerivative` is a non-reducible integral-defined function, plain `simp` cannot get this by unfolding.
findings.proposed_change: Add `@[simp]` to `logDerivative_initial` (together with `position_initial`). Then the `Initial_deficit` step at lines 353-355 and the similar calls in ConditionalTilts, LoewnerFlow and AngularClock reduce to `simpa using …` with at most the `LoewnerExit.radius`/`sine` unfoldings. The RHS is the literal `0`, so there is no loop risk, and the LHS is a function application whose only reducible form is the integral, which the lemma avoids.
findings.benefit: `simp` reaches the same normal form `radius … 0 = ·` as the hand-written list, without each caller repeating the pair of lemma names. Proofs about initial conditions become more robust to changes in the definitions of `radius` and `sine`.
